title: Fatal police shooting justified: ASIRT
article: Two Edmonton police officers were justified in shooting and killing Bernadette Auger, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team said Wednesday.
The 48-year-old woman was shot by both officers on Jan. 16 at an Edmonton apartment.

She was holding an air-gun replica of a Sig Sauer handgun which was painted black. Auger was not responding to police commands, police said. Cliff Purvis, executive director of ASIRT, said the officers acted lawfully, and their actions were justified.
Police were called to the walk-up apartment at 119th Avenue and 84th Street just after 2 p.m. after a 911 call about a woman carrying a gun.
Auger met the officers on the second-floor landing, pointing what police said appeared to be a pistol at them.

The officers retreated outside. When Auger came out of the building a short time later, she walked directly toward the officers still holding the pistol. Each officer fired two shots at her when Auger didn't respond to their commands.
Auger was taken to hospital where she was pronounced dead.
Purvis said their investigation revealed Auger was intoxicated at the time of the shooting. She had a blood alcohol content three times the legal limit for driving, he said.

"I've concluded that it would have been impossible to identify the pistol she was holding as a toy, as opposed to a real firearm," Purvis said. "I've concluded that the police officers involved in this officer-involved shooting, acted lawfully and their actions were justified."
